briefs.episode_title: Stripe, Visa, Mastercard, Microsoft, Meta. All Building The Same Thing.
briefs.channel: AI News & Strategy Daily | Nate B Jones
briefs.one_line_summary: The internet economy is shifting power from sellers to buyers through agentic commerce, necessitating a focus on making businesses usable by customer agents.
core_claims: Power in the internet economy is shifting from the seller to the buyer.
Stripe's new agent commerce products aim to build economic infrastructure for the agentic economy.
The next competitive question for companies is whether their business can be called by agents, not just whether they use AI.
Agentic discovery prioritizes software usability over traditional search ranking, enabling businesses to broadcast inventory and commercial capabilities directly into agent interfaces.
briefs.positioning_implication: Focus on structuring data and operations to be readily accessible and understandable by AI agents, enabling seamless integration with agent-driven commerce ecosystems.

briefs.episode_title: This Is the Biggest Risk to the U.S. Economy Right Now | Anthony Scaramucci & Michelle Makori
briefs.one_line_summary: Political tribalism and the resulting lack of long-term planning pose the biggest risk to the US economy.
core_claims: AI could displace 20% of white-collar jobs, leading to economic anxiety and political instability.
Accidental strengthening of the dollar due to war has increased international funds into the US stock market.
Markets are pricing in a resolution to geopolitical conflict and anticipating exponential increase in productivity due to AI.
The stock market is currently at 250% of GDP indicating it is overpriced, however it's delivering the earnings.
Debt outside of the US balance sheet is now equal to the US GDP.
A four-day work week will emerge as AI increases productivity, creating new leisure-based job markets.
briefs.positioning_implication: Acknowledge the potential for economic dislocation due to AI, while also anticipating potential upside from increased productivity and new job markets.

briefs.episode_title: Gold & Silver Building Price Momentum: This NEW RECORD Shows Why!
briefs.one_line_summary: Central bank gold buying sets a record despite pullback, indicating continued metals bull market momentum.
core_claims: The relationship between gold and the U.S. dollar shows gold's 2020 top coincided with the dollar bottoming out, and gold's 2023 reversal correlated with the DXY falling.
Central banks have bought the dip in gold every time since 2022, with 2022 being the largest year for central bank purchases.
Central banks bought 367 metric tons of gold in the first quarter, making it the fourth largest quarter for gold purchases by central banks on record.
In the first quarter of 2026, central banks set a new record, spending $37 billion acquiring gold for reserves, which is 55% more than what was spent in quarter three of 2022.
The market is already pricing in a scenario of no more rate cuts in 2026 for gold and silver.

Price targets here on the right side of the screen with gold getting above $7,000 an ounce, and silver getting between $150 and $200 an ounce is where we should be expecting gold and silver to move in the next phase up.
briefs.positioning_implication: Increase exposure to gold and silver assets, anticipating further gains based on central bank activity and US dollar trends. Monitor central bank gold purchases for confirmation.

briefs.episode_title: Buy Income On The Cheap | Steven Bavaria
briefs.one_line_summary: High-quality publicly traded BDC funds are currently undervalued, offering attractive income investment opportunities.
core_claims: Individual BDCs with large discounts are definitely undervalued.
Income factory strategies can achieve average equity returns (9-10%) with bond-like safety through high-yield credit and reinvestment.
Income factory aims to provide consistent 8-9% returns, even amidst paper losses, and capital appreciation is a bonus.
Bavaria's personal portfolio generates a 12% interest yield with an annualized total return of 9% due to some capital erosion.
Some private credit funds are priced as if there will be 50-70% default rates, which is likely overstated.
briefs.positioning_implication: Consider shifting portfolio allocation towards undervalued BDCs and income-generating assets to capitalize on high yields and mitigate market volatility.
